newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai firm's debt default sparks jitters.
newsitem.headline: Thai firm's debt default sparks jitters.

text.p: Thai investment firm One Holding Plc's default on debt has aroused fears that other weak Thai business and property firms may succumb to liquidity shortages as the country's economy slows.
Market analysts said on Wednesday One Holding's repayment default on its matured $13.5 million bills of exchange came amid a struggle by some Thai property companies to meet their debt obligations.
The One Holding's default was the third by a Thai company in recent months.

Thai furniture maker STA Group last October sought a delay in repaying its 1.1 billion baht debentures sold to the public. In February, Housing developer Somprasong Land Plc failed to make a $3.1 million interest payment on its Euroconvertible debenture.
"The market watch is more on property firms, on whether they could adjust and ride out the current crisis," said an analyst at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities Co.

The analyst said most property developers would likely try to survive their four-year business slump by doing what Juldis Develop Plc did -- selling land and assets at deep discounts to raise funds to pay off debts.
"My concern is that the One Holding default may be followed by similar cases in the property sector," said an analyst at Multi-Credit Corp of Thailand Plc.
The analysts said, however, that the One Holding default should be viewed as an isolated case, saying it was a fallout from the merger of its parent Finance One Plc with Thai Danu Bank Plc.
"In normal circumstances, Finance One would have helped out One Holding regardless of liquidity problems that the parent company itself may be facing now," the Chao Phaya analyst said.
She said Finance One's failure to back One Holding confirmed that the unit was left out of the Finance One-Thai Danu merger deal.
Finance One owns a 9.91 percent stake in One Holding's 340 million baht capital. One Holding posted a 217.5 million baht net loss in 1996 against 224.8 million baht profit in 1995.
One Holding, in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand on Tuesday, blamed the extended Thai stock market slump and tight money market liquidity for its first debt default.
An analyst estimated that One Holding's securities portfolio carried an unrealised loss of about one billion baht at end-1996.

"One Holding is a debtor of Finance One with a balance of about 1.0 billion baht for loans and bills of exchange. However, Finance One holds sufficient collateral to cover the entire amount," Finance One told the Thai bourse.

"One Holding gets its earnings solely from equity capital gains and dividends. Under the current condition, these earnings have not only disappeared, their underlying assets have also sharply shrunk in size," the MCC analyst said.
The Thai stock market has retreated about 46 percent in the past year.
